reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that probability emerges from bounded knowledge rather than inherent randomness. Epistemic ignorance underpins all probabilistic reasoning, forming a kernel of uncertainty that must be modeled mathematically. Deterministic causality fails when full measurement is impossible, leading to stochastic models. The paradox of homogeneity reveals that real-world groups are never perfectly uniform, necessitating variance-aware inference. These primitives form a triadic structure: ignorance → causality → heterogeneity. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian belief updates on incomplete data; in GSE, it governs state transitions through probabilistic logic. Each primitive has a dual role: one in modeling uncertainty, another in shaping decision pathways.
